newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures close down on export concerns.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures close down on export concerns.

text.p: UK grain futures closed lower on Wednesday on concern over European Union (EU) export subsidy policy.
"The market was begining to looking over done after the recent rally and the word from the Commission did nothing to help matters," said a trader.
EU Commission Director-General David Roberts said earlier the EU would have to pursue a cautious grain export subsidy policy for the rest of 1996/97 (July-June) due to budgetary problems.
Roberts noted that current EU wheat export subsidies were running at about five times higher then the average level of 4.25 Ecus a tonne included in the draft 1997 budget.
"On the basis of what has been said, I don't think we are going to get much joy out of the weekly grain tenders from now on," said another trader.
Wheat futures closed 0.25 to 1.80 stg down after trading 709 lots while barley was 0.50 to 0.65 stg lower on 30 lots.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures were unchanged and tradeless. --Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8062
